results.alertTitle: Multiple failed logon attempts against SOC-FW-RDP

summary.tpReason: The pattern is consistent with a high-rate automated password-spraying/brute-force attempt: 11,970 failures in one hour against 257 names, with broad generic/local-admin, backup, and multilingual account-name enumeration. Concurrent campaigns hit SHIR-Hive and SHIR-SAP, supporting an active scan rather than a user mistyping credentials.
summary.fpReason: The event data does not retain source address, logon type, failure status, or process attribution, so an approved test cannot be conclusively excluded. However, the volume, account dictionary, and multi-host targeting are not consistent with routine user activity.
summary.whatHappened: From 2021-10-23 05:26:19Z through 06:25:57Z, SOC-FW-RDP recorded 11,970 Event ID 4625 failures against 257 account strings. Attempts heavily favored \ADMINISTRATOR (9,997), then \ADMIN (503), \USER (269), \TEST (263), and \SERVER (240), with many generic, backup-product, and multilingual names. No source IP is populated in SecurityEvent and no matching RDP/firewall connection was present in CommonSecurityLog. The only 10 Event ID 4624 successes on SOC-FW-RDP were NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM; there was no successful targeted user logon. The same time window shows failed-logon bursts on SHIR-Hive (5,704) and SHIR-SAP (489), also with only SYSTEM successes.
keyEvidence: SOC-FW-RDP logged exactly 11,970 Event ID 4625 failures from 05:26:19Z to 06:25:57Z, spanning 257 accounts; the dominant names were ADMINISTRATOR (9,997), ADMIN (503), USER (269), TEST (263), and SERVER (240).

The account list contains typical automated RDP enumeration targets, including ADMINISTRATOR/administrator, ADMINISTRADOR, ADMINISTRATEUR, VEEAM, BACKUPEXEC, AZUREADMIN, VMADMIN, and many generic user names.
During the campaign window, all 10 Event ID 4624 events on SOC-FW-RDP were NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. No attempted account had a successful logon.
The same burst timing affected SHIR-Hive (5,704 failures) and SHIR-SAP (489 failures); their only Event ID 4624 successes were also NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

Observed scheduled-task modifications on SOC-FW-RDP were attributable to SYSTEM/NETWORK SERVICE and referenced standard Microsoft UpdateOrchestrator and SoftwareProtectionPlatform tasks, not an attacker-created task.
researchDone: Reviewed SecurityEvent authentication events on SOC-FW-RDP from 05:00Z-07:00Z and broader 2021-10-22 through 2021-10-24 context; failures occur only in the one-hour alert period.
Aggregated Event IDs 4624/4625 by account and examined all successful logons during the campaign; only SYSTEM succeeded.
Checked the two concurrent hosts, SHIR-Hive and SHIR-SAP, for successful logons during the same activity; only SYSTEM successes were observed.
Queried CommonSecurityLog for SOC-FW-RDP, its hostname/device name, and RDP port 3389 during 05:00Z-07:00Z; no matching network records were available.

Reviewed task-creation/update and related security events on SOC-FW-RDP; observed task content was standard Windows Update/Software Protection activity, with no evidence of post-authentication account creation, privilege change, audit clearing, or persistence.

Reviewed SecurityAlert records for the period; the only related alerts were failed-logon campaigns on SOC-FW-RDP and SHIR-Hive. A separate audit-log-clear alert was on win11a and was not linked by host or account.
